AL.t: A state law effective Oct. 1 makes regulators test whether contracts with data centers of 150 MW and up cover their full cost, and the PSC now votes on them publicly. Towns from Birmingham to Fort Payne have paused, and Bessemer voters ousted council members who approved the 1,200 MW Project Marvel.

AR.t: No statewide rules, and a 2023 law limits how far cities can restrict data centers. Counties have adopted some of the longest pauses in the country, five years in Independence County, while Little Rock twice rejected a moratorium on 4–4 ties.

AZ.t: A June law lets regulators set minimum bills and contract terms for very large customers, and the budget stopped new data center sales tax exemptions until mid-2029. The attorney general is challenging utility deals for Project Blue, and Pima County paused development outside Tucson.

CA.t: Seven laws signed Sept. 21 cover grid cost tariffs, water supply assessments, energy and noise reporting, labor standards and an end to blanket environmental review exemptions. No statewide moratorium. Locally, Monterey Park, Coachella and Calexico ban data centers, Los Angeles County, San Francisco, Oakland and dozens of cities have paused, and Alhambra votes on a ban Nov. 3. San Jose and Santa Clara chose rules instead.

CO.t: Lawmakers killed both a data center incentive bill and a large-load regulation bill in May, so the action is local: Denver, Mesa County and more than a dozen other jurisdictions have paused. Regulators are reviewing Xcel's data center tariff.

CT.t: No new state rules. Bills to end the 2021 data center tax break and set large-load rules died, though Gov. Lamont says the state is the wrong place for massive AI campuses. West Haven and Morris have paused, and New Haven is weighing a pause.

DE.t: Gov. Meyer signed bills in August making large data centers pay their own grid costs through regulator-approved contracts, bring their own power within 10 years, and give up job-based tax credits. Regulators had already paused new large hookups, and a state ruling blocked half of the 6-million-square-foot Delaware City project. New Castle and Kent counties have set zoning limits.

FL.t: The Florida Hyperscale Data Center Act, signed in May, makes facilities of 50 MW and up pay their full cost of service and preserves local power to say no; utilities filed data center rates by Oct. 1. More than 20 counties and cities have since paused or banned, including outright bans in Volusia, Wakulla and Escambia counties.

GA.t: Regulators let Georgia Power charge data centers over 100 MW for grid costs, but the legislature again left the sales tax break, now projected at $2.5 billion a year, intact. Dozens of counties have paused, and two Public Service Commission seats are on the Nov. 3 ballot.

IA.t: A data center reporting and tariff bill died without a floor vote, leaving the action to counties and cities, several of which have paused.

ID.t: 2026 laws require regulator-approved contracts for new loads of 50 MW and up and restrict consumptive water cooling at new data centers. A bill to narrow data center tax breaks died.

IL.t: Gov. Pritzker ordered the state to stop processing new data center incentive agreements in June and is pressing for his POWER Act in the fall session. Regulators let ComEd scale deposits for large loads, and more than a dozen communities have paused or hold advisory votes Nov. 3.

IN.t: HB 1210 makes data centers share tax savings with local governments, and regulators have approved large-load contracts for Google and Amazon campuses. Indianapolis paused permits through 2027; Fort Wayne rejected a pause.

KS.t: Regulators approved Evergy's large-load tariff with minimum bills and collateral in 2025. Emporia and El Dorado vote Nov. 3 on some of the strictest local bans in the country.

KY.t: Gov. Beshear's August executive order bars passing data center costs to other ratepayers, after lawmakers stripped similar protections from a bill. Regulators must approve co-op data center contracts. Meta is behind a 1.2 GW Mason County proposal. Lexington, Louisville, Oldham and Daviess counties have paused, Mercer County rejected rules that would have allowed hyperscale sites, and Woodford County became the first in the state to ban data centers permanently.

LA.t: The region's most pro-development state: a 20-year tax break, fast-tracked gas plants for Meta's Hyperion campus, and a 3–1 regulator vote to keep Meta's power and jobs data secret. New Orleans bars data centers until mid-2027, and two regulator seats are on the Nov. 3 ballot.

MA.t: Gov. Healey paused the data center sales tax exemption in June, and Executive Order 658 bars state permits without local approval and a community benefits agreement. Holyoke banned data centers; Lowell, Westfield and Mansfield have paused or set rules.

MD.t: A 2025 rate negotiation law is on the books, an emergency statewide moratorium stalled, and the governor created a task force in September to review every project of 25 MW or more. Counties are the real action: Harford banned data centers outright, and Anne Arundel, Baltimore County and Baltimore City have paused.

ME.t: Came closest to the first statutory statewide moratorium before Gov. Mills vetoed LD 307 to protect a project in Jay. Since then more than ten towns, including Sanford, Bangor and Brunswick, have paused, and three towns vote on bans or pauses Nov. 3.

MI.t: Senate bills would impose a one-year statewide moratorium, and Attorney General Nessel is challenging DTE's data center contracts. Kalamazoo, Lansing, Flint and other towns have paused, while Van Buren Township approved Google's 1 GW campus.

MN.t: Regulators approved Xcel's very large customer tariff with stiffer exit terms in May, and the 2026 session added no new restrictions. The attorney general opposes Xcel's Google power deal as filed, and about ten local governments have paused.

MO.t: No state action logged yet, but about a dozen counties and cities have paused, including Pettis County for up to two years.

MS.t: No statewide limits; a 2024 law gave data centers sweeping tax breaks. The fight centers on xAI's gas turbines in Southaven: a state permit, a NAACP Clean Air Act suit a judge let proceed, and a neighbors' noise suit. Jackson paused approvals in July.

MT.t: The 2025 Right to Compute Act limits government restrictions on data centers, and a 2025 law extended property tax incentives to 2037. Missoula County adopted the state's first moratorium in July, and a legislative committee is drafting ratepayer protections.

NC.t: More than 30 jurisdictions have paused, including Charlotte, Raleigh, Durham and Greensboro, though a court challenge undid Chatham County's pause. Duke Energy filed a large-load tariff settlement with tech companies in October, and regulators denied a Duke gas plant over uncertain data center demand.

ND.t: The House refused to take up a data center permitting moratorium in a September special session, and the Senate killed a ban on nondisclosure agreements. Lawmakers are drafting a 2027 bill on power, water and decommissioning.

NE.t: Gov. Pillen's July executive order set up a data center task force on water and environmental impacts, with recommendations due to lawmakers by 2027.

NH.t: The House killed a one-year statewide ban in March, but Gov. Ayotte now opposes any data center in the state and plans a multi-year moratorium in her next budget; House Democrats want 24 months. A utility study eyes a large load at Bow's former coal plant.

NJ.t: A July law puts data centers of 50 MW and up in their own rate class, and an August law requires twice-yearly water and energy reports. Advocates count about 110 towns that have banned data centers, and a developer is suing Monroe Township for $300 million.

NM.t: The fight is over Project Jupiter in Doña Ana County: the state supreme court rejected challenges in September, while the attorney general contests its air permit and gas pipeline review ahead of a Dec. 7 permit hearing. Several local governments have paused.

NV.t: Gov. Lombardo's September order makes data centers seeking tax breaks pay school taxes in full and cover their power costs, and lawmakers are drafting a bill to end the breaks. Reno paused permits and Nye County banned data centers around Pahrump. Boulder City votes on a land transfer area in November.

NY.t: First statewide permitting pause, by executive order. Hochul's EO 62 freezes discretionary state environmental approvals for data centers of 50 MW and up while regulators study impacts. A broader legislative moratorium (20 MW) passed in June and sits on her desk until Dec 31. More than a dozen towns, from Brookhaven to Allegany, have also paused or banned data centers.

OH.t: Regulators and a 2025 law put data centers on their own tariff, Gov. DeWine halted review of new data center tax exemption requests in May, and regulators tightened AEP Ohio's terms. Ohio leads the country in local ballot measures, and a statewide ban amendment is aiming for 2027.

OK.t: SB 1488's statewide moratorium died without a vote. Tulsa and Oklahoma City paused new data centers through 2026, and the Cherokee Nation and the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes have barred large data centers on tribal lands.

OR.t: Effectively a statewide pause. On Oct. 9 Gov. Kotek told regulators to stop issuing air and water permits for new or expanded data centers until July 1, 2027, after pausing state land deals. Regulators raised PGE data center rates 29.7% under the POWER Act. Hillsboro, Salem, Woodburn, Forest Grove and Clackamas County have paused, while Umatilla and Hermiston say the state pause is costing them millions. Both governor candidates back a statewide moratorium, and Democrats plan a three-year moratorium bill.

PA.t: Gov. Shapiro turned his voluntary GRID standards into binding permit conditions by executive order in August: projects of 25 MW and up must sign a consent order, pay their full grid costs and win local approval before state permits issue. House committees are advancing cost and interconnection bills. The House voted 197–5 to repeal the data center sales tax break, and Archbald denied two hyperscale campuses this year.

RI.t: All six data center bills died in June, and none proposed a statewide moratorium. Smithfield banned data centers in every zone, and Westerly and Hopkinton have paused.

SC.t: A 2025 law adds ratepayer protections, but 2026 permitting and moratorium bills died. Spartanburg County froze projects over 65 MW, and a settlement bans data centers in most of Colleton County's ACE Basin.

SD.t: Statewide moratorium talk ended in a local-control law. Two companion bills signed in March let counties and towns regulate or ban data centers.

TN.t: A 2026 law makes data centers of 50 MW and up pay for grid upgrades but lets them build their own power, and in August the Tennessee Valley Authority created a data center rate class that raises their rates about 10% on average over three years. Memphis rejected an 18-month moratorium on a tie, then passed a 135-day pause; Nashville, Knox County, Knoxville, McMinnville and others have paused.

TX.t: The biggest reversal of the year. Gov. Abbott, who called Texas the epicenter of AI development in 2025, froze new grid approvals pending an ERCOT audit in August, then halted state environmental permits in September. Cities and counties that tried their own pauses have been sued or rescinded them.

UT.t: Gov. Cox's May executive order sets a higher bar for large data centers, and lawmakers are studying a bill to define them. Fights over the Stratos project's water and discharge permits are ongoing, and several local governments have paused.

VA.t: The largest market wrote the densest package: a first-in-the-nation tax on data center electricity use, cost-allocation rules for loads of 25 MW and up, tighter generator and water rules, and a regulator order making data centers pay for dedicated transmission. The sales tax exemption survived, for now. Locally, Prince William ended by-right approvals, QTS terminated the Digital Gateway, and Loudoun votes Nov. 17 on a 12-month pause. Moratorium bills are filed for 2027.

VT.t: Lawmakers passed rules for large data centers, but Gov. Scott vetoed them and the veto stood; S.205's moratorium never left committee. Royalton and Morristown have since blocked data centers locally, and a poll found two-thirds support for a statewide ban.

WA.t: SB 5982 holds data centers to the state clean-energy law, and lawmakers trimmed the sales tax break, but the broader HB 2515 died in the Senate. Seattle, Spokane and Spokane, Snohomish, Pierce, Yakima, Benton and Skamania counties have paused. Klickitat County has not, despite six hyperscale proposals, and Grant PUD wants higher data center rates around Quincy. A statewide moratorium bill is expected in 2027.

HI.t: No data center fights at the state level, where the energy office is studying the issue. Hawaii County is weighing Bill 170, which would make industrial-scale data centers a non-permitted use on the island; its two planning commissions split on it.

AK.t: The state is courting data centers, offering a North Slope land lease for a campus that could draw up to 3 GW from local gas. A Senate-passed ratepayer bill died in the House. The Democratic candidate for governor backs a moratorium until lawmakers write rules; the leading Republicans favor development.

WI.t: Regulators approved Meta's Beaver Dam power deal with conditions and ordered a standard tariff, and a settlement commits the DNR to a statewide impact study. A statewide moratorium bill failed, Republicans propose repealing the sales tax break, and Milwaukee voted for a one-year pause.

WV.t: The 2025 Power Generation and Consumption Act strips counties of power over certified data centers and their private power plants, and sends most of their property tax to the state. Efforts to restore local control stalled in 2026.

WY.t: Gov. Gordon's June executive order sets state expectations for data centers, and regulators rejected an attempt to treat a data center power project as a non-utility. A committee narrowly killed a bill exempting some generators from utility rules.
